title: Control plane: add burst config schema + validation + migration
author: Benji Okafor
description: Context: Dedicated Burst capacity needs a control-plane owned configuration object that can be validated, audited, and safely rolled out per tenant/region without impacting existing Dedicated tenants. This PR introduces the initial burst config schema (protobuf + JSON), validation + defaulting rules, a forward-only migration for storing the new config, and unit tests covering key edge cases. This is intentionally scoped to schema/storage/validation only (policy evaluation + routing integration are in ENG-4823/ENG-4824). What’s included: (1) New proto schema: DedicatedTenantBurstConfig + BurstLimitOverrides. (2) JSON API surface: /v1/dedicated/tenants/{tenant_id}/burst with read/write (internal-only for beta; Console will follow). (3) Validation: guardrails around limit ranges, allowlists, and region scoping; safe defaults that preserve current behavior (burst disabled unless explicitly enabled). (4) Migration: adds a burst_config blob column + updated config versioning, with backfill = NULL / disabled. (5) Unit tests: schema round-trip, validation table tests, migration apply/rollback semantics (rollback is a no-op per migration framework; this is consistent with other config migrations). Schema overview (proto excerpt): message DedicatedTenantBurstConfig { bool enabled = 1; repeated string eligible_regions = 2; repeated string eligible_pool_labels = 3; BurstLimitOverrides limits = 4; string updated_by = 5; int64 updated_at_unix_ms = 6; } message BurstLimitOverrides { uint32 max_concurrency = 1; uint32 max_tokens_per_second = 2; uint32 max_requests_per_second = 3; uint32 max_burst_duration_seconds = 4; uint32 cooldown_seconds = 5; } Notes/decisions: - We store the raw config as a typed proto in the control-plane config store, but the API also supports JSON for operator tooling; both map to the same canonical proto. - Field naming follows existing Dedicated tenant config conventions (snake_case in JSON; proto field names are lower_snake, generated structs are idiomatic in Go). - Defaulting rules: enabled defaults to false; eligible_regions defaults to empty (treated as ‘no regions eligible’ rather than ‘all’) to avoid accidental global enablement; limits default to per-environment safe defaults but are only applied if enabled=true. - Validation is strict on beta: unknown eligible_pool_labels are rejected (to avoid silently routing to non-burst pools); we can relax later if needed. - Audit logging is NOT in this PR (ENG-4833), but we include updated_by/updated_at in the schema to make later audit logging and UI display straightforward. - INT-881: added a small helper in the admin API to return a 403 with actionable text when a caller lacks burst admin permission; permissions enforcement itself remains in the existing RBAC layer. Testing: - go test ./controlplane/... (unit + validation suites) - migration test harness: controlplane/migrations TestMigrate_BurstConfigColumnAdded - protobuf JSON roundtrip: TestBurstConfig_JSONRoundTrip. Rollout plan: behind feature flag controlplane.features.burst_config_api (default off). When enabled, write paths remain restricted to internal service accounts used by ops tooling. Follow-ups: - ENG-4823 policy evaluation will consume this config (region-aware eligibility + cap evaluation). - ENG-4833 will add full audit log emission for config writes and policy reads. - Docs/Console wiring will follow once we have end-to-end pilot enablement.
commits: controlplane: add burst config proto + codegen
controlplane: implement burst config validator + defaulting
tests: add validation table tests + json roundtrip
review_conversation: Ethan Park (review): Overall looks good. Two concerns: (1) eligible_regions defaulting to empty could be confusing—can we make it explicit in docs/errors? (2) max_tokens_per_second should have an upper bound to prevent overflow/DoS in downstream calculations. Benji Okafor (author): Added explicit validation error message when enabled=true and eligible_regions empty (‘no eligible regions configured; burst will never admit’) and added upper bounds for TPS/RPS + max_concurrency aligned with current router limits. Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): Please ensure RBAC denial message doesn’t leak internal permission names to customers. Also, can we record who updated the config? Benji Okafor: Denial message now uses generic ‘burst admin permission required’ string (no internal scope names). Added updated_by/updated_at fields to schema; wiring of actual audit log emission is in ENG-4833 but write path now populates these fields from caller identity. Jordan Lee (review): Validation should reject unknown pool labels for determinism; also, JSON mapping should be stable (snake_case). Benji Okafor: Implemented allowlist check against fleet label registry (cached) and enforced JSON snake_case via the existing marshaler config; added a roundtrip test asserting stable key casing. Chloe Martin (review): Any impact to Console? Also, migration safety in multi-region control planes? Benji Okafor: Console unaffected (flag off; endpoint is internal-only). Migration is additive (new nullable column) and guarded by config store version; tested in staging with multi-writer enabled. Approvals: Ethan Park approved after changes; Kaitlyn Nguyen approved; Jordan Lee approved.
release_notes: Internal: adds control-plane burst config schema + validation + storage migration (feature-flagged; no customer-visible behavior change).
